subject: english
question:
The following sentence has been split into three segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

Don’t panic! / We won’t leave you alone in trouble / when you travelling with us.

options.text: We won’t leave you alone in trouble

solution:
The correct answer is **"When you travelling with us".**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• In time clauses with words like **when, after and until,** we often use **present tense forms **to talk about the future:
 
• **For example:**
 
 
• I'll come home **when I finish work.**
 
• You must wait here **until your father comes.**
 
• They are coming **after they have had dinner.**
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct sentence would be: **Don't panic! We won't leave you alone in trouble when you travel with us. **

Therefore, the correct answer is **"Option 1".**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **"Don’t panic!"** – This sentence is free from any grammatical mistakes.

 
 
• It's a command or an imperative sentence and is grammatically correct.
 
• The subject (you) is understood and does not need to be stated explicitly.
 
 
 
• **"We won’t leave you alone in trouble" – **This sentence is also error-free.
 
 
• The phrase **'We won't' **is a contraction for **'we will not' **which is grammatically correct.
 
• **'Leave' **is a proper base form of the verb to use after **'will not.' **
 
• The rest of the sentence, **'you alone in trouble,' **correctly follows standard English grammar rules.
